description: Whether each registered provider (schemas.StandardProviders) sends its requests to network_config.base_url (TXE-7083). "honours": base_url replaces the vendor host. "fallback": a key-level host wins and base_url applies only without one. "ignores": the host comes from elsewhere (host_from) and base_url changes nothing, so a fixture config must redirect it as "fixture" says. tests/e2e/api/runners/lib/base-url-support.test.mjs fails when a registered provider is missing here, when a provider whose package never reads BaseURL is not "ignores", and when a fixture config sets base_url on an "ignores" provider. In an offline run (scripts/test-offline.sh) a request to any non-loopback host fails anyway, naming it.

azure.host_from: azure_key_config.endpoint on the key (a full URL; http:// is accepted)
azure.fixture: set azure_key_config.endpoint to the fixture, e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:8791"

bedrock.host_from: bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com (and bedrock., bedrock-agent-runtime., s3.) built from bedrock_key_config.region; requests are SigV4-signed for that region
bedrock.fixture: set bedrock_key_config.endpoints.runtime (control_plane, agent_runtime, mantle, s3 as needed) to a loopback TLS listener such as "127.0.0.1:8793" (the provider error fixture's TLS port) and network_config.insecure_skip_verify: true; Bedrock always dials https://, and the fixture does not check signatures

bedrock_mantle.fixture: set bedrock_mantle_key_config.endpoints.mantle to a loopback TLS listener and network_config.insecure_skip_verify: true, as for bedrock

vertex.host_from: <region>-aiplatform.googleapis.com (or aiplatform.googleapis.com for global) built from vertex_key_config.region; OAuth goes to Google's token endpoints
vertex.fixture: no host override exists: cover Vertex with Go tests that swap the provider's client, and keep it out of fixture configs (an offline run refuses its hosts, naming them)

huggingface.fixture: set network_config.base_url to the fixture; the model hub lookup (GET <base_url>/api/models/<model>) follows it too (TXE-7117), so the fixture must answer that route as well as the inference one

databricks.host_from: databricks_key_config.workspace_url on the key; network_config.base_url applies only when the key has none
databricks.fixture: set databricks_key_config.workspace_url to the fixture's host:port

azurespeech.host_from: azure_key_config.endpoint on the key, else network_config.base_url; either may be a region name (eastus), which becomes the Azure Speech host for that region, or a resource endpoint URL
azurespeech.fixture: set azure_key_config.endpoint (or network_config.base_url) to the fixture's full URL, e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:8791"; a bare region name always reaches Azure
